title: Friendship
content:
"I was born in Bengaluru and completed my schooling there," Siddu began, his voice calm and steady. "Later, I moved to Mysore for my intermediate studies."

A faint smile appeared on his face as he gazed out of the window.

"Mysore... it's a beautiful city. Peaceful streets, pleasant weather, and greenery everywhere. It didn't take long for me to fall in love with the place."

He paused for a moment before continuing.

"I had always been an above-average student in the MPC stream, so I started searching for a good college. After a lot of research, I finally got admission to one of the reputed colleges in Mysore."

His smile slowly faded.

"But the day I stepped into that college... I felt completely out of place."

He let out a quiet laugh.

"Almost everyone around me looked like they came from wealthy families. Their clothes, the way they spoke, even the confidence they carried—it all made me feel small."

"I, on the other hand, came from a simple middle-class family. We didn't have much, but my parents had worked hard to give me a good education."

"I remember exactly what I was wearing that day—a blue checked shirt and a pair of black trousers."

"I found my classroom, walked in quietly, and settled into the last bench. Since I didn't know anyone, I simply sat there, observing every face that entered the room while waiting for the first class to begin."

A few minutes later, just as the lecturer was about to start the class, the sound of bangles gently echoed through the silent classroom.

Almost instinctively, I looked toward the door.

A girl had just walked in.

She had a graceful medium complexion and was dressed in a simple blue outfit that perfectly matched the golden earrings swaying gently with each step she took. There was nothing extravagant about her appearance, yet something about her effortlessly drew my attention the moment she entered the classroom.

The lecturer noticed her the moment she stepped into the classroom.

"Why are you late?" he asked, looking at her over his glasses.

"Sorry, sir," she replied politely. "I got stuck in traffic."

He sighed with a helpless smile.

"That's the excuse I hear every single day. Anyway, go and take your seat."

She nodded and glanced around the classroom. Every bench was occupied.

Every bench...

Except the one beside me.

As she began walking toward the last bench, my heartbeat grew louder with every step she took. Before I could gather my thoughts, she had already taken the empty seat beside me.

For a moment, I forgot that the lecturer was teaching.

"Hi," she said with a gentle smile before turning her attention toward the class.

I wanted to reply with confidence, but all I managed was a nervous nod before pretending to focus on the lecture.

The entire period passed like that. I listened to the lecturer, but my mind wandered back to the girl sitting beside me more often than I cared to admit.

When the bell finally rang for the break, the classroom instantly came alive with conversations.

Summoning every bit of courage I had, I turned toward her.

"What's your name?" I asked.

She smiled.

"I'm Shreya. And you?"

"Siddhartha."

"Nice to meet you, Siddhartha."

With that, she walked out of the classroom to join the others, leaving me with a smile I couldn't seem to wipe off my face.

Days slowly turned into weeks.

What had started as a simple introduction soon blossomed into a close friendship. Along with Kiran and Rohini, the four of us became inseparable. We attended classes together, shared lunch, teased one another, studied before exams, and filled every ordinary day with laughter.

Somewhere along the way, without even realizing it, my feelings for Shreya began to change.

She had become much more than just a friend.

Every smile of hers made my day brighter, and every conversation with her became the highlight of my day.

Yet I never found the courage to tell her how I truly felt.

I was afraid.

Afraid that if I confessed my feelings, I might lose the beautiful friendship we had built together.

So I buried those emotions deep within my heart and chose to remain silent.

"One evening during the break, I was standing by the classroom window, watching the sun slowly disappear beyond the horizon. The sky was painted with shades of orange and crimson, and for a few peaceful moments, nothing else seemed to matter."

"I didn't even realize someone had walked up beside me until I heard her voice."

"It really is beautiful, isn't it?" Shreya said as she sat beside me, admiring the sunset.

I smiled and nodded.

For a while, neither of us spoke. We simply watched the evening sky together.

Then, gathering a little courage, I turned toward her.

"Shreya... are you committed?"

She looked at me for a moment before smiling.

"No."

The answer sent a wave of happiness through me, though I did my best not to let it show.

She tilted her head playfully.

"What about you?"

I smiled.

"No. I'm not committed either."

She looked at me from head to toe before letting out a soft laugh.

"Really? Not even a single girl likes this handsome face? That's hard to believe."

Then she looked away before I could read her expression.

I chuckled.

"I'm telling the truth."

She simply smiled and nodded.

"Okay... I'll believe you."

Just then, Kiran and Rohini joined us, and the conversation drifted to other topics as the four of us spent the rest of the break together.

But her words refused to leave my mind.

"Not even a single girl has fallen for this handsome face?"

If she really thought I was handsome... then why hadn't she ever shown any feelings for me?

The question lingered in my heart for days.

In the end, I convinced myself that I was only overthinking.

Whatever I felt for Shreya, I decided to keep it locked inside my heart. I didn't want to risk losing the friendship that meant so much to me.

Days passed peacefully.

Until one incident changed everything.

...

Siddu fell silent before continuing.

Just then, the train jerked gently as it began slowing into the next station.

Both of them glanced out of the window before stepping onto the platform to stretch their legs. The cool breeze and the lively atmosphere offered a welcome break from the long journey. They walked quietly along the platform for a few minutes before the whistle echoed through the station, signalling departure.

They returned to their seats just in time.

As the train began moving again, Sneha turned toward Siddu with an eager smile.

"So..." she said softly, her curiosity evident in her eyes, "...what happened next?"
